record.title: Brothers in Arms (Fraternization)
record.scan_source: Photogrammetry scan; exact open-licensed Objaverse archive version Atrium removed captured lawn and grass billboards around the granite pedestal; no sculpted surfaces were reconstructed.
record.note: A Soviet soldier and a Czech partisan embrace at the end of the Second World War. The same composition’s Prague cast later became part of the city’s queer social history, as discussed by art historian Pavel Karous. This model records the Saint Petersburg version; that reception offers a further reading of the adult men’s public affection without replacing its original liberation narrative.
record.attribution: Brothers in Arms (Fraternization). Artwork: Karel Pokorný. 3D model: FelixMatveev; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry optimized for browser display.

context.title: Brothers in Arms / Brotherhood
context.context: Pokorný’s embracing adult soldier and partisan commemorate liberation. The same composition’s Prague cast has acquired queer reception and appears in Teplá Praha as a gay meeting place.

sources.supports: Czech public radio interview with sculptor Pavel Karous; explicit gay reception of the Prague cast and original nonsexual liberation subject.
Prague City Gallery confirms original composition1947–1950, soldier and partisan embracing. Different cast from this scan.
Jan Šindelář’s scholarly history of the composition,2020; historical commissioning and casts, not proof of queer intent.

context.limits: The local St Petersburg nickname is an uploader claim. Attribute the documented queer reception to the Prague version/same composition, not automatically to this particular cast; do not claim the historical figures were lovers.

exhibition_placements.caption: Carved after Girona’s plague epidemic, this panel belonged to a larger altarpiece dedicated to Saint Sebastian. Painted flesh and gilded surfaces make his bound body vivid. The isolated panel preserves the central image while the surrounding altarpiece has been lost.

Two women remove their garments in the circular field inside the cup. Tilt the vessel to see how the painted scene follows the shallow bowl, then compare it with the figures on the outside. This digital reconstruction records both image and container; the scene’s precise meaning remains uncertain.

Carved wood, paint, and gilding work together: relief gives the body and tree their depth, while color distinguishes skin, cloth, and setting. Side light reveals a different order of details from the one established by the painted surface.

Hermes bends toward his sandal while turning his attention outward. The lifted foot and twisting torso suggest a task interrupted. Move around the figure to see how the support stabilizes the body while the head redirects its movement.

Hercules wrestles Achelous after his rival has taken the form of a serpent. The hero’s bent legs brace the struggle while the coils pull the action in another direction. Different views clarify the grip and the distribution of weight.

The missing head and arm belong to the sculpture’s physical history; they are not gaps created by the 3D viewer. The surviving dog, drapery, and stance still help identify Meleager. The fragment shows how much an attribution can depend on what remains beside a body.

An ancient ivy-crowned head has been joined to a modern bust. The mount gives the portrait a complete presentation without restoring its original body. Look at the transition below the neck: the figure now seen is also a record of later collecting and display.

Spartacus led resistance to the society that had enslaved him. Foyatier gives the rebel the monumental nude body usually reserved for celebrated heroes. Set beside images of imperial conquest, this figure asks whose struggle receives dignity and whose freedom is treated as a threat.

Achilles’s anger begins with the loss of Briseis, a captive treated as a prize in the struggle between Greek commanders. Bissen concentrates the drama in the hero’s tense body. The woman at the center of the dispute remains outside the image, reminding us whose experience heroic narratives can omit.

1989, using a sculpture modeled in 1963–1964. Hrdlicka’s inverted Marsyas forms part of a memorial to victims and opponents of fascism, racism and war. The broken wall and exposed body give public remembrance a language of injury. Here the classical figure carries the burden of twentieth-century violence.

The kneeling figure throws both arms upward as its weight sinks. Compare the immense modeled strength of the body with the loss of control suggested by its pose. This bronze was cast in 1961 after a model developed in 1940–1942.

data.scope: Independent four-angle review of sheets 1–4. Root owns sheet 0. Decisions combine visible asset quality with separately stated adult-subject and identity holds.

items.title: Thor
items.reason: All four views show a complete seated figure, support and base. No conspicuous missing surface or frame clipping.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult divine figure. Primary museum source identifies plaster; scan text says marble and should be corrected.

items.title: Meleager
items.reason: The head, right arm and dog head are historically missing, confirmed against the Art Institute scholarly photograph of Glyptotek 1562. Torso, drapery and limbs are coherent in all views. Rear base has ragged scan edges; this minor base issue must be disclosed separately from the genuine ancient losses.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult heroic body; confirmed historical fragment.
items.followup: Inspect rear base edge in final larger render; cleanup may remove loose fringe, but must not invent missing sculpture.

items.title: Hermes
items.reason: Complete bent figure, drapery, legs and support in all four angles. No significant scan holes visible.
identity_or_age_flags: Sandal-fastening Hermes, not infant-bearing Hermes.

items.title: Herakles
items.reason: Clean, closed torso fragment with consistent fracture boundaries across views. Absent head, hands and lower legs read as historical losses, not camera clipping.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult muscular torso; use fragment title.

items.title: Bacchus or satyre
items.reason: Headless draped figure has coherent front and rear surfaces; the neck/limb terminations look like physical breaks. No material 3D scan loss visible in reviewed angles.
identity_or_age_flags: Bacchus or satyr remains uncertain. Source calls him a young man; do not assert a numerical age.
Physical-fragment reference still desirable before final labeling.

items.title: Satyr with panther
items.reason: Mesh itself appears complete, but the scholarly museum source identifies the satyr as adolescent. Exclude from this adult-focused erotic selection.
identity_or_age_flags: Subject-age rejection, not scan-quality rejection.

items.title: Head of a Satyr, 1st century
items.reason: Front face is detailed, but rear contains a large flat faceted cavity/cap with abrupt polygonal boundaries. Without a physical-object rear reference, an accurate complete head fragment cannot be distinguished from a filled scan hole.
identity_or_age_flags: MIA 2006.110 / object 81221; adult bearded face.
items.followup: Could be reconsidered if museum rear photography confirms this unusual physical shape; otherwise do not hide it by choosing only a frontal hero.

items.title: 1974.16 Kottabos Element Of A Dancing Satyr
items.reason: Thin limbs, raised arm and perforated circular support survive in all angles. No evident capture holes. The upper dish is a documented historical loss.
identity_or_age_flags: Bearded adult satyr. Exact same-sex context remains weak and separate from visual acceptance.

items.title: Young Satyr drinking Wine
items.reason: The scan is visually intact, but the figure has youthful proportions and the formal title Vinsugende Satyrdreng identifies a satyr boy. Exclude from this adult-focused selection.
identity_or_age_flags: Subject-age rejection, not scan-quality rejection.

items.title: Statuette eines Schwerathleten
items.reason: Mesh is an intelligible historical fragment, but the old title misidentifies the subject: the museum now calls it a female gladiator. No sufficient same-sex interpretation has been established for this batch.
identity_or_age_flags: Identity/context rejection, not scan-quality rejection.
Update title if acquired in a later non-thematic batch.

items.title: Sculpture of Hercules for Metateca Project
items.reason: Back view repeats a reversed view of the face and chest through the absent rear surface. Side views show a thin partial shell and ragged boundary; complete sculpture was not captured.
identity_or_age_flags: Do not relabel a sculpture in the round as a relief to conceal an incomplete scan.

items.title: Bust of Commodus as Hercules
items.reason: Rear head/lion-skin and bust are substantially open; shoulder, torso and base have large ragged gaps. These are scan losses rather than the intended bust termination.

items.title: Hercule combattant Archeloüs
items.reason: All four views show continuous figure, snake, arm and plinth geometry. Recognizable small details are somewhat softened by reconstruction, but no major missing components.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult Hercules with serpent-form Achelous; not a pair embracing.
Identify scan/model repair lineage accurately.

items.title: Theseus Minotaur
items.reason: The two figures, raised arm, contact points and stepped base are coherent in all angles. No major missing geometry or clipping.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult hero and mythological Minotaur; bodily combat is not evidence they are lovers.

items.title: Dionysos and Pan
items.reason: Complete standing figure, staff, smaller bearded Pan, panther and base. All contact regions appear continuous.
identity_or_age_flags: Pan is a small adult mythological figure, not automatically a child due to scale; verify museum identification.

items.title: Bacchus, Satyr, panter
items.reason: Both bodies, lifted cup, supporting contact and base remain legible in every view. No scan holes apparent.
identity_or_age_flags: Museum documents old physical restorations. Youthful idealization should not be assigned a numerical age without evidence.

items.title: El-Kantara male torso
items.reason: Model is a coherent closed historical torso, but the primary collection identifies Ptolemy V as Horus with a sidelock of youth, a crowned child. Exclude from this adult-focused erotic batch.
identity_or_age_flags: Subject-age rejection, not scan-quality rejection.
Correct old generic El-Kantara male torso title.

items.title: Male Torso
items.reason: Torso and draped rear are complete as a fragment; visible drilled holes and breaks appear physical. Small square display/scan base remains, with only minor edge fringe.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult-looking torso fragment; no precise age established.
Same-sex interpretation is comparative rather than documented for this exact object.

items.title: Faunus
items.reason: Whole bronze figure and square support are present; face/front appears in view 3. Default view is nearly side-on.
identity_or_age_flags: Strongly stylized satyr with childlike rounded torso: age is not secure visually. Hold erotic framing unless adult subject interpretation is supported.
No exact queer context has been established.

items.title: Glyptothek Satyr
items.reason: Figure, leaning support and drapery are legible from all angles. Hollow tree/support details are described in source metadata and should not be treated as scan damage.
identity_or_age_flags: Youthful idealized satyr; do not conflate with the Barberini Faun or infer a secure age from type alone.

items.title: Rodin - The Three Shades
items.reason: Model is sideways and embedded in a large ragged captured ground plane with scattered debris. Figures are coarse and partly fused/indistinct at review scale. This needs substantial reconstruction/cleanup beyond a hero orientation fix.
items.followup: Reconsider only after a clean upright render isolates all three complete figures; current asset is not publication ready.

items.title: Neptune - Louvre Museum
items.reason: Neptune, sea creature, drapery, arm and base are legible from all sides; default view faces the back. Opposite view presents face and chest cleanly.
identity_or_age_flags: Scan source warned of capture limitations, but no major gap is visible in these four renders.
items.followup: Inspect held rod/trident against source photo before claiming all original attributes survive.

items.title: Mercure monté sur Pégase - Louvre Museum
items.reason: Mercury, Pegasus, wings and rocky support remain recognizable in all angles. Base rim has torn scan edges and several small holes, strongest in rear end-on view; main sculpture appears intact.
identity_or_age_flags: Minor scan defects are in support/base edge, not visibly in the main human figure.
items.followup: Clean loose base fringe and inspect final larger render before publication; do not claim a watertight mesh.

items.title: Sculptre of Hercules from Royal Łazienki
items.reason: Adult figure, lion and plinth appear complete. Default angle is nearly profile; view 2 presents chest, face and action clearly.
identity_or_age_flags: Physical head restoration should be noted from museum metadata.

items.title: Aurore (Les Vagues)
items.reason: Adult two-woman composition and main surfaces are complete; use the opposite angle to show their fronts. A small clean oval at the resting wrist/thigh may be a physical negative space. The available museum reference confirms the larger arm/body openings but does not resolve this smaller opening from the same angle.
identity_or_age_flags: Adult figures; interpretation may be curatorial without claiming artist intention.
items.followup: Second visual judgment requested from root before final acceptance; do not assume the wrist opening is missing scan geometry. Source scan predates the documented 2022 repair of cracks and one nose.
items.root_resolution: Root independently compared reference and scan and accepted the small wrist/thigh opening as natural negative space. Label the scan as the pre-2022-restoration state.

items.title: Kylix with Two Women Putting Aside Their Garments
items.reason: Vessel body, foot, lip and two handles appear complete, but all four low views conceal the interior scene. Use a more elevated hero camera so the intended subject can be seen.
identity_or_age_flags: Label as a digital reconstruction of a painted vessel, not a scan of sculpted figures.
Confirm the interior texture exists and its adult figure interpretation against the museum image.
items.followup: Render elevated view; recommended vector deliberately increases camera elevation beyond the four standard review presets.

data.scope: Independent review of all four root-generated views for six extra candidates; no asset or catalog mutation

items.title: Antinous Mondragone
items.reason: Rear scalp and neck are replaced by a large smooth artificial cap, interrupting the detailed curls. The Louvre records an in-the-round sculpture; small historic chips and missing eye inserts do not account for this broad absent surface.

items.title: Spartacus
items.reason: Figure, supporting drapery, arms and legs are coherent in all four views. No major missing geometry visible. View 2 presents the torso more clearly than the default.

items.title: Perseus Holding the Head of Medusa
items.reason: Separate tall display pedestal has a badly reconstructed rear. Remove the display pedestal beneath the sculpture’s small integral plinth, then render again. The upper raised Medusa/head area is low-detail and should be checked at the improved framing; approval remains conditional.

items.title: Neptune at Dyrham
items.reason: The figure is small within an oversized grass-and-pedestal capture, with soft fused detail in the raised arm and drapery area. A weak thematic candidate also, so this source is not recommended for this batch. The missing trident is historic according to the National Trust and is not itself a scan defect.

items.title: Neptune, Valencia
items.reason: Figure, trident prongs, limbs and marine support are readable from all four directions without major holes. Surface lighting varies, but the model is coherent. Context remains a weak comparative reading; visual acceptance does not recommend thematic inclusion.

items.title: Doryphoros, Mia
items.reason: Coherent full 360-degree representation of the actual fragmentary sculpture. Missing left forearm, fingers and nose are documented physical losses. View 3 presents the front.

data.scope: Independent visual review of four angles for five modern candidates and the Nymphs relief. Conditional flags distinguish physical fragments from missing scan geometry. No catalog or asset mutation.

items.title: Nymphs of the Spring
items.reason: The relief has a coherent sculpted front, rough stone back and full block edges. All four adult female figures and their overlapping limbs remain readable. The back is deliberately unworked stone, not an artificial cap.

items.title: Marsyas II memorial
items.reason: The figure, brick wall, rear wall and slab are coherent in all four views. The statue occupies a small part of the full memorial, so a closer front-facing poster may help. No major missing geometry visible at current resolution.
items.optional_cleanup: Trim only extraneous pavement outside the memorial slab if needed; preserve wall and memorial context.

items.title: L’Accident de carrière
items.reason: Higher-resolution 600×750 close review after reversible ground removal reveals torn faces and major voids through the supporting workers’ legs/arms and the carried figure’s shoulder. The primary reference confirms the composition, but does not justify these missing scanned surfaces. Ground cleanup cannot repair the artwork.
items.audit_history: Contact-sheet-scale provisional acceptance was overturned by the mandatory close inspection after cleanup.

items.title: Priam Pleads with Achilles
items.reason: The rear shows the front relief reversed; this is a front shell without the physical marble slab’s rear. The edge views expose extremely shallow, incomplete capture. It fails the current complete-3D filter despite a usable front.

items.title: Statue of Male Figure, Hunt Museum
items.reason: The full surviving torso and display base are coherent from all four directions. Head and limbs are historical losses per the museum’s source description. Thin protrusions at the rear/side resemble old mounting or restoration pins, not giant missing faces; confirm from primary object image before retaining them. No major scan holes visible.
items.curatorial_note: A generic torso with no exact queer reception established; lower priority for this focused batch.

items.title: Mbapete
items.reason: Both adult-looking wrestlers, their limbs and the carved base are coherent around all four views. Rough faceting is consistent throughout the limestone treatment. No major scan holes apparent. A primary identity/source record is still needed.
